To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the N6-dATP residue of a DNA duplex reacts with an AP site to form a dA-AP interstrand cross-link, and the structure of the dATP-AP cross-link was determined.
(1) the dA- AP ICL forms between an N6-dAdA base pair and an AP site in the opposing strand and (2) the structure of the d A -AP ICL is consistent with the unhooking mechanism proposed for NEIL3.

we have determined the structure of a DNA interstrand cross-link formed by the reaction between a nucleophilic N-6 amino group of adenine and the aldehyde of an AP site, and that this structure provides insight into the mechanism by which the DNA glycosylase, NEIL3, can unhook this cross-link during replication.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural characterization of the ICL formed by an AP site in the context of an oligodeoxynucelotide sequence.
the structure, stability and biological significance of DNA cross-links.
the structure of DNA ICLs and how they can be repaired.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dA- AP ICL structure is a consequence of the interplay of the chemical and physical properties of DNA and that it is not an artifact of the experimental procedure.
the N6-dAdA-AP ICl is an ordered structure that is stabilized by stacking of flanking A9-T29 base pairs, and that the β configuration of the AP site is stabilized by the N6-dadA amino group.
the structure of the stable ICL formed between a dA and an AP site is consistent with the proposed mechanism for the unhooking of this ICL by NEIL3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure of the d(A)-AP ICL has been determined and that the structure is compatible with a model of the NEIL3 dA-AP glycosylase activity.

the NMR data presented herein provide a detailed molecular description of an ICL that can be replicated, as opposed to ICL structures that are not amenable to replication, such as the dA-dA cross-link.
the NMR spectroscopy has revealed the structure of a stable DNA cross-link involving an N6-dATP-AP ICL.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure of the dG-AP and dA-AP interstrand cross-links are very similar.
the dA-αAP ICL is structurally distinct from the dA-βAP ICL.
the dA- AP ICL is an ordered DNA structure with a stable β-N-glycosyl linkage between the AP site and the dA residue.
